newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac, Jordan's Hassan stress access to Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: Chirac, Jordan's Hassan stress access to Jerusalem.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac and Jordan's Crown Prince Hassan expressed concern on Wednesday that all faiths should be guaranteed access to Jerusalem as part of the Middle East peace process.
"The president and the prince expressed the same concern on the question of Jerusalem," a French official said after talks between the two men in Paris.
"Freedom of access for all believers must be guaranteed, not merely preserved, under the future status of Jerusalem," the official said.
Palestinians see East Jerusalem, captured by Israel in the 1967 Six-Day war, as the capital of a future independent state. Israel has vowed to keep control of the city.
Jerusalem is sacred to Moslems, Christians and Jews.
Hassan recalled that "the treaty between Jordan and Israel recognises a special role for Jordan over the Islamic holy places in Jerusalem," the official said.
Chirac, who has argued for an independent Palestinian state, clashed with heavy-handed Israeli security guards in East Jerusalem during a visit in October.

Prince Hassan said the "atmosphere was better" in peace talks and underlined "the importance of continuing the peace process with the Palestinians, but also between Israel and its neighbours," the French official said.
Chirac praised Jordan's efforts in helping foster compromise between Israelis and Arabs and also hailed Hassan's efforts in promoting talks between different religions.
Hassan was due to meet French Roman Catholic cardinal Jean-Marie Lustiger and Jewish leaders during his visit to France. REUTER
